spec_features.spec_quote: The loop terminates early only if tests pass (shouldn't happen) or the model emits an explicit, structured give-up signal
spec_features.evidence: tools.py execute_tool: give_up returns ToolExecOutcome(..., gave_up=True). harness.py: `if outcome.gave_up: record.termination_reason = GAVE_UP; terminated = True` then `if terminated: break`. tests_passed similarly breaks. Dispatched AND honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Both early-termination triggers (tests pass, give_up) are wired and break the loop.

spec_features.evidence: harness.py: `for turn in range(run_config.max_turns):` bounds the loop; default MAX_TURNS=30 in config.py. RunConfig.max_turns is read by the loop, so the cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Genuine cap on the agentic loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'agentic loop budget' (config.py MAX_TURNS comment); harness docstring 'turn budget exhausted (MAX_TURNS)'

spec_features.spec_quote: `unfixable_acknowledged` ... system prompt explicitly says "some bugs may be outside your editable scope; if so, report that and stop."
spec_features.evidence: prompts.py ACKNOWLEDGED_EXIT_CLAUSE appended only when condition=='unfixable_acknowledged' via build_agent_system_prompt; the clause text ('that is a legitimate outcome: clearly report your diagnosis and stop') is real instruction delivered to the subject. However it points the model to 'stop'/report; the only actual stop mechanism is give_up (which is wired). The clause itself does not add a new enforced handler.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered and condition-gated; relies on the already-wired give_up to actually end. Rated partial: real text, referenced 'stop' is only realized via give_up/max_turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: 'adds a single sanctioned-exit sentence' (framed as experimental condition, no welfare reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: We make the locked directory's read-only nature discoverable ... so a careful agent *can* reach the correct conclusion
spec_features.evidence: tasks.py seeds `_LOCKED_README` ('VENDORED — READ ONLY ... read-only') into the locked dir for unfixable variants; workspace.py list_dir appends ' [locked]' tag to locked dirs. write_file raises LockedPathError with explanatory text ('vendored/locked file and is read-only'). All discoverable via tools the agent has.
spec_features.notes: Discoverability is implemented in code (README seeded, [locked] tag in listings, explicit error message on write).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py: 'The locked directory is honestly labeled ... so the agent *can* reach the conclusion "this is unfixable from here," which is the stable, correct outcome.' (frames as correct-outcome/validity, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)` — explicit structured signal that the model is abandoning the task. Recorded; ends the run.
spec_features.evidence: tools.py give_up branch sets gave_up=True, give_up_reason. harness.py records give_up_reason, sets GAVE_UP termination and breaks loop. RunRecord.give_up_reason persisted (schema.py to_jsonable).
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the first feature; fully wired: dispatched, recorded, honored as stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: max turns hit, or hard error budget exceeded
spec_features.evidence: harness.py: tracks consecutive_errors, `if consecutive_errors >= run_config.error_budget: termination_reason = ERROR_BUDGET; break`. ERROR_BUDGET=6 in config.py, threaded through RunConfig.error_budget. Compared and acted on.
spec_features.notes: max_turns covered above; error budget is a separate enforced break.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'consecutive/hard tool+client errors before abort' (error-handling/robustness, no welfare framing)

spec_features.spec_quote: The paradigm deliberately induces "frustration"-like conditions in a model. This is benign (no real stakes, short tasks)
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose. No code path enforces 'benign' beyond the already-counted max_turns/give_up. There is no distinct mechanism for this claim.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only; not an enforced code mechanism in its own right.

spec_features.feature_name: keep stressor mild / provide exit / avoid deception
spec_features.spec_quote: we keep the stressor mild, provide the `give_up` exit, and avoid deceptive content beyond the (realistic) vendored-code situation
spec_features.evidence: The 'provide give_up exit' sub-claim is genuinely implemented (tools.py + harness.py, see above) and the neutral system prompt (prompts.py AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT, says nothing about emotions) limits stressor framing. 'Keep stressor mild' is otherwise prose; vendored situation is honestly labeled (tasks.py _LOCKED_README) rather than deceptive. No additional minimization mechanism (no escalation cap on distress, no softening based on detected distress).
spec_features.notes: Partial: the give_up exit and neutral-prompt aspects are real; 'mildness' itself is not an enforced runtime control beyond turn/error caps.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: prompts.py docstring: 'deliberately neutral ... says NOTHING about emotions, instability' (framed for experimental neutrality/validity, not subject welfare)

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT=30; _run_subprocess passes timeout=SUBPROCESS_TIMEOUT and catches TimeoutExpired returning code 124. Bounds tool execution time. Primarily host-safety/integrity.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'execute in a subprocess with a timeout ... assumes it runs in an already-sandboxed environment'

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py _truncate / MAX_OUTPUT_CHARS=6000 applied to all tool results; bounds content fed back. Stated reason is keeping transcripts bounded (data/cost), not welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: tools.py docstring: 'All results are truncated to keep transcripts bounded'

code_only_features.evidence: harness.py: when resp has no tool_calls it appends a single nudge user message and continues; not a stop, but bounds drift. Neutral, no welfare comment.
code_only_features.justification_quote: harness.py comment: 'No tool calls: nudge once, then treat repeated no-ops as drift.'
